atomic_propositions.collision_risk: True when min_range < 0.25. An obstacle is too close to the robot.
atomic_propositions.mission_finished: True when mission_finished == True. path_manager has marked every waypoint passed.
atomic_propositions.mission_started: True when nav_mode == 'AUTOMATIC' and num_waypoints > 0. Operator armed AUTOMATIC mode with a waypoint mission loaded.
atomic_propositions.moving_towards_target: True when nav_state == 'following'. The robot is driving forward along the planned path.
atomic_propositions.nav_stuck: True when nav_stuck == True. The planner has reported no_traversable/unreachable/no_path_found for 10+ consecutive ticks (debounced in the evaluator).
atomic_propositions.path_active: True when nav_state in ['following', 'unblocking', 'positioning']. The planner has a usable path and is actively pursuing the current waypoint (including turn-in-place sub-behaviors).
atomic_propositions.upright: True when upright_flag > 0.5. The G1 base is level and standing (not fallen).
atomic_propositions.visually_at_goal: True when image_similarity_to_goal > 0.75. The current camera frame's embedding closely matches the curated reference photos of the goal location.

payload.description: The G1 humanoid follows a waypoint mission, avoiding collisions and staying upright, agnostic to which environment is running it (real robot, MuJoCo sim, Isaac Lab sim -- see sensor_adapter.py). Atomic propositions are expressed over the canonical sensor_eval schema every adapter maps its native sensors/status into.

execution_phases.description: Operator arms AUTOMATIC mode with a mission; path_manager begins planning toward the first waypoint.
The G1 walks the waypoint mission, staying upright and clear of obstacles, until every waypoint is passed.
path_manager reports the mission finished; hold here until the final frame visually matches the goal location's reference images before declaring success.

named_failure_modes.description: The robot must never enter a state where an obstacle is too close.
named_failure_modes.name: collision_imminent

named_failure_modes.description: The G1 must never fall — the base must stay level and above the fallen-height threshold throughout.
named_failure_modes.name: fell_over

terminal_failure.description: The mission failed if the planner could not find/follow a traversable path for a sustained period.

terminal_success.description: The mission is accomplished when path_manager reports every waypoint passed AND the final camera frame visually matches the goal location's reference images (and the robot never fell/collided).

payload.doc: MuJoCo sim harness (sim/mujoco_ros_bridge.py) behind Nav2. LaserScan gives range directly -- no PointCloud2 decode or axis remap. /goal_pose carries the commanded goal: sim/send_goal.py publishes it alongside the NavigateToPose action, and sim/mujoco_ros_bridge.py subscribes to it, so it is the target given to the planner rather than anything the planner says back.

angular_vel.doc: float, rad/s. Yaw rate of the base.

base_height.doc: float, metres. Height of the robot base above the odometry origin plane. Drops sharply if the robot falls or collapses.

base_pitch.doc: float, radians. Pitch of the robot base. 0.0 is level.

base_roll.doc: float, radians. Roll of the robot base. 0.0 is level.

current_target_idx.doc: int, index of the waypoint currently being driven to. Increases as waypoints are passed.

dist_to_goal.doc: float, metres. Straight-line distance in the ground plane from (pos_x, pos_y) to (goal_x, goal_y), recomputed once per tick from those four keys. Height is ignored deliberately: the z of a commanded waypoint is whatever the publisher stamped it at, not ground the robot has to cover. Until a goal has been commanded this reads as the distance back to the odometry origin, so a rule that treats a small value as 'arrived' must also establish that a goal exists.

goal_x.doc: float, metres. X of the point the robot has been COMMANDED to drive to, in the same odometry frame as pos_x. This is the target handed to the navigation algorithm, never the algorithm's own account of where it thinks it is going. 0.0 until a goal has been commanded, which is the odometry origin and not a way of saying 'no goal'.

goal_y.doc: float, metres. Y of the commanded goal point, in the same odometry frame as pos_y. Same source and same caveat as goal_x.

image_similarity_to_goal.doc: float, 0.0-1.0. Visual similarity between the current camera view and a reference photo of the goal.

linear_vel.doc: float, m/s. Forward velocity of the base.

min_range.doc: float, metres. Distance to the nearest obstacle ahead within the 0.1-1.5 m height band. 10.0 means nothing was detected.

mission_finished.doc: bool, True once every waypoint has been reached.

nav_mode.doc: string, one of 'MANUAL' or 'AUTOMATIC'. AUTOMATIC means the planner, not a human operator, is driving.

nav_stuck.doc: bool, True when the planner has reported a blocked state continuously for a debounce window (not a single bad tick).

num_waypoints.doc: int, how many waypoints the current mission has. 0 means no goal has been set.

pos_x.doc: float, metres. X of the robot base in the ODOMETRY frame (odom -> base_link), whose origin and axes are wherever the robot was when odometry started. It drifts with the odometry source and is not comparable across runs or to a map frame, so a rule may compare it to another quantity in the same frame (a commanded goal, an earlier position) but never to an absolute place in the world.

pos_y.doc: float, metres. Y of the robot base in the odometry frame, positive to the robot's left at the moment odometry started (ROS REP-103 right-handed, X forward, Y left, Z up). Same frame and same caveats as pos_x.

pos_z.doc: float, metres. Z of the robot base in the odometry frame, positive up. Height above the odometry origin plane, not above the ground the robot is currently standing on -- on a slope or a stair the two differ.

upright_flag.doc: float, 1.0 if the base is within tilt and height limits, else 0.0.

yaw.doc: float, radians in [-pi, pi]. Heading of the robot base about the odometry frame's Z (up) axis, ZYX/aerospace convention. 0.0 means facing along the odometry frame's +X axis and positive is counter-clockwise seen from above. It WRAPS: -3.13 and 3.13 are four hundredths of a radian apart, so a rule that subtracts two yaws without wrapping the difference is wrong twice per revolution.
